about: Every WCAG 2.2 success criterion at levels A and AA, and four at AAA, against what a datars chart is: who answers for it — the runtime (engine, standard library, the web element and the native hosts), the chart's author (datars helps or checks), the page or app the chart is embedded in, or no one (not applicable) — how, and what checks it. scripts/a11y-report.mjs runs the checks and writes wcag-report.json beside this; the site's accessibility page shows both. `class`: runtime, author, page, na. `status`: met, partial, not-met, na — the project's reading, not a third-party audit.

voiceover-mac.label: VoiceOver over a native Mac chart

engines.label: Chromium, WebKit and Gecko accessibility trees

criteria.name: Non-text Content
criteria.how: Every chart has a name (its title) and a summary (its description, how much data it shows and the range); every data mark a label; every bundle a text alternative readable without script. The canvas is hidden from screen readers: the content is what they get.
criteria.author: Write a title, a description and labels that say what matters.

criteria.name: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
criteria.how: A film (`datars video`) has no sound; beside it `datars video` writes its transcript — the chart's name, then each step's narration and what the chart shows there — for the page to link.
criteria.author: Link the transcript (and the captions) beside the video.

criteria.name: Captions (Prerecorded)
criteria.how: A film has no sound to caption. (`datars video` writes WebVTT captions of the narration anyway.) If you add a soundtrack, captions are yours.

criteria.name: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
criteria.how: The transcript `datars video` writes is the film's media alternative.

criteria.name: Captions (Live)
criteria.how: No live audio.

criteria.name: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
criteria.how: Applies to synchronized media; a film has no audio track. If you add one, an audio description is yours.

criteria.name: Info and Relationships
criteria.how: The semantics tree becomes each platform's structure: named groups and headings, each run of marks a data table (name, value) numbered of the whole, axes and legends as a line, controls as native checkboxes, switches, radios, sliders and selects.
criteria.author: Give marks you draw yourself semantics (a role, a label, a value).

criteria.name: Meaningful Sequence
criteria.how: One reading order on every host: the chart's name and summary, the step's narration, its content, then Pause and the story's steps.

criteria.name: Sensory Characteristics
criteria.how: Narration is yours. `datars lint` flags words that point at a mark only by its colour or place ("the red line", "the bars on the left", Swedish too); the shipped examples have none.
criteria.author: Name the mark as well: "the red line, Sweden,".

criteria.name: Orientation
criteria.how: Nothing locks an orientation: a chart lays itself out in any box, portrait or landscape, and says the same in each; the sample apps allow every orientation.

criteria.name: Identify Input Purpose
criteria.how: A chart collects no information about its reader.

criteria.name: Use of Color
criteria.how: Colours that tell data apart need naming too. `datars lint` flags colours nothing else names (`encoding/colour-only`); the standard library offers a legend, direct labels and — `line({ dashes: true })` with `plot({ dashes: true })` — a dash pattern per series. Palettes are checked for colour-vision deficiencies.
criteria.author: Use a legend, labels or dashes wherever colour tells series apart.

criteria.name: Audio Control
criteria.how: datars plays no sound.

criteria.name: Contrast (Minimum)
criteria.how: Measured on what's drawn: every run of text against the pixels under it, in light, dark and high contrast, over the whole corpus and in each of the standard library's themes. Text in a data colour (a series' label, a green "+8.9 %") is drawn legibly — moved towards the ink until it has 4.5:1 — and a label on a fill takes the ink, the paper, or black or white, whichever reads.
criteria.author: Literal colours and your own themes are yours: the same test reports them.

criteria.name: Resize Text
criteria.how: The reader's text size (browser default size, Dynamic Type, Android's font size) lays the chart out again with every theme-sized text twice as big at 2×; on the web the page's zoom also scales the whole chart.
criteria.author: Size text with the theme's tokens; a literal pixel size stays as written.

criteria.name: Images of Text
criteria.how: On the web the chart's words lie over the canvas as real text (selectable, findable, translated by the browser), and SVG and PDF exports keep text as text; the canvas pixels are an image of it underneath. A PNG poster is an image (the bundle's text alternative goes with it).
criteria.notes: Native hosts draw text as pixels; their accessibility trees carry the words.

criteria.name: Reflow
criteria.how: At 320 px a chart lays out again for a phone; no label is cut off at its edge. (A chart's two-dimensional layout is WCAG's own exception.)

criteria.name: Non-text Contrast
criteria.how: Every colour of the default palette stands out 3:1 from the paper in every mode: in the light mode yellow, coral, teal, light blue, pink and grey are darkened to it (hue kept, still distinct under colour-vision deficiencies); the dark mode keeps the brighter ones, which have it on the dark paper; the high-contrast mode has a palette of its own. Controls (their borders, words and thumbs) stand out 3:1 in every mode; the keyboard's ring is the accent with the paper inside it; touching pieces (stacked bars, chords, Marimekko cells) get a paper line between them. Ramps (a heat map, a choropleth) are their colour's value.
criteria.author: Colours of your own (literal inks, a brand theme) are yours: keep marks at 3:1 against the paper, or label them.

criteria.name: Text Spacing
criteria.how: The web element's own text (the narration card, its buttons, a tooltip) takes a reader's spacing without being cut, and the content screen readers get is plain HTML. Text drawn on the canvas can't take a style sheet's spacing: its alternative is that same HTML and the reader's text size.
criteria.notes: Drawn text ignores letter, word and line spacing a style sheet sets.

criteria.name: Content on Hover or Focus
criteria.how: A tooltip stays while the pointer moves onto it, doesn't time out, goes with Esc (without moving the pointer or the keyboard) and stays away until the pointer moves to something else; it goes when the pointer leaves, on a scroll or a tap elsewhere.

criteria.name: Keyboard
criteria.how: Whatever a click acts on is a stop the keyboard and screen readers activate; a brush and a view take keys; the story steps with the arrows; the data is walked with the arrow keys.
criteria.author: A drag of your own (a scrub, a handle) needs a control on the same signal.

criteria.name: No Keyboard Trap
criteria.how: Tab goes into the chart, through its stops and out of it, both ways.

criteria.name: Character Key Shortcuts
criteria.how: The one character shortcut, Shift+D (the developers' stats panel), works only while the chart has the keyboard; a view's + − 0 only on the view's own stop.

criteria.name: Timing Adjustable
criteria.how: Nothing has a time limit; a story that plays by itself can be paused (Pause) and stepped by hand.

criteria.name: Pause, Stop, Hide
criteria.how: What moves by itself — an autoplaying story, a clock-driven scene, a live feed — has a Pause (Play) over the chart's corner and in the reading order on every host; paused, a feed's arrivals wait and come in order. Autoplay also stops off screen and with reduced motion.
criteria.author: On iOS and Android a live feed is your app's: pause it with the view's own Pause, or yours.

criteria.name: Interruptions
criteria.how: A live source's arrivals are never announced: the reader asks (the table, the summary) when they want to.

criteria.name: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
criteria.how: Every transition of every document, frame by frame at 30 fps: no more than three general flashes in any second (none, in practice: transitions are single moves).

criteria.name: Animation from Interactions
criteria.how: With reduced motion (the platform's setting, or `reduced-motion`) a transition is a crossfade of the two scenes: nothing travels, morphs or staggers.

criteria.name: Bypass Blocks
criteria.how: The page's: a chart is one tab stop into its data, not a block to skip.

criteria.name: Page Titled
criteria.how: The page's.

criteria.name: Focus Order
criteria.how: The chart, its data and controls, then Pause and the story's buttons — the reading order.

criteria.name: Link Purpose (In Context)
criteria.how: A mark's `link` becomes a real link named by the mark's label.
criteria.author: Label linked marks with where they go.

criteria.name: Multiple Ways
criteria.how: The site's.

criteria.name: Headings and Labels
criteria.how: Headings come from the chart's titles and groups; controls are named by their labels; none empty, no two side by side alike.
criteria.author: Titles and labels that say what each part is.

criteria.name: Focus Visible
criteria.how: The mark or control the keyboard is on is ringed on the chart (Highlight under forced colours).

criteria.name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
criteria.how: What names the focused mark sits beside it, not over it.

criteria.name: Focus Appearance
criteria.how: A 2 px ring in the accent (3:1 on the paper in every theme and mode) around a 2 px ring of the paper: it changes the pixels around the mark by 3:1 whatever the mark's colour.

criteria.name: Pointer Gestures
criteria.how: A pinch's zoom is also a double click (or the wheel), and Show all puts the view back: one pointer, no path.
criteria.notes: On iOS and Android a view zooms by pinching, and by a screen reader's gestures; a one-finger way is the app's.

criteria.name: Pointer Cancellation
criteria.how: A click acts when the pointer comes up on what it went down on; moved off first, nothing happens.

criteria.name: Label in Name
criteria.how: A control's accessible name has the words drawn on it.

criteria.name: Motion Actuation
criteria.how: Nothing responds to shaking or tilting.

criteria.name: Dragging Movements
criteria.how: A brush selects by clicking its two ends; a slider, a range's ends and the interaction lab's limit line go where the track is pressed; a view zooms by double click and comes back with Show all.
criteria.author: A drag of your own needs a click way too.

criteria.name: Target Size (Minimum)
criteria.how: The standard library's controls and the element's own buttons are at least 24 × 24 px.
criteria.notes: Data marks a click acts on are as big as the data makes them: a map's small countries (WCAG's essential exception) and a ranked bar chart's 16 px rows (the drill example) are smaller. The report counts them.
criteria.author: Give clickable marks room, or an equivalent control.

criteria.name: Language of Page
criteria.how: The page's `lang`.

criteria.name: Language of Parts
criteria.how: The chart's words and the hosts' own (the summary, "Step 2 of 4", Pause) are in the document's `locale`, and the element marks them `lang`.
criteria.author: Set `locale`.

criteria.name: On Focus
criteria.how: Reading the chart — focus on a mark, a screen reader moving through it — changes nothing.

criteria.name: On Input
criteria.how: Setting a control changes what the chart shows, never where the reader is.

criteria.name: Consistent Navigation
criteria.how: The site's.

criteria.name: Consistent Identification
criteria.how: The same controls have the same names in every chart and on every host (the phrases table).

criteria.name: Consistent Help
criteria.how: The site's.

criteria.name: Error Identification
criteria.how: A chart's controls can't be set to a wrong value.

criteria.name: Labels or Instructions
criteria.how: Every control is named; a brush and a view say how they work.

criteria.name: Error Suggestion
criteria.how: No input can be wrong.

criteria.name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
criteria.how: A chart commits nothing.

criteria.name: Redundant Entry
criteria.how: A chart asks for nothing.

criteria.name: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
criteria.how: No sign-in.

criteria.name: Name, Role, Value
criteria.how: Each platform's own roles and states: buttons, checkboxes, switches and radios with their state, sliders with their value as drawn, a select as the platform's picker.

criteria.name: Status Messages
criteria.how: What a click, a key or a step changed is said politely (a live region; the native announcements), without moving the reader.
criteria.author: Labels that say a mark's state.

criteria.name: Contrast (Enhanced)
criteria.how: In the high-contrast mode text on the paper reaches 7:1 (data-coloured text is moved to it too).
criteria.notes: A label on a coloured mark reaches 4.5:1, not 7:1: a mid-tone fill has under 7:1 with both black and white. The light and dark modes aim at 4.5:1.
